newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan seen taking big Q4 charge. [CORRECTED 19:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: MacMillan seen taking big Q4 charge. [CORRECTED 19:05 GMT]

text.p: MacMillan Bloedel Ltd is poised to report a sharp fourth-quarter loss and hefty special charges, with the news likely to increase shareholder pressure for a big shake-up at Canada's biggest lumber and paper maker.

MacMillan is forecast to report next Tuesday a fourth-quarter operating loss of C$0.10 to C$0.25 a share or C$13 million to C$31 million. Special charges would add C$0.32 to C$0.44 a share or C$40 million to C$55 million to that, analysts said.
In the same period a year earlier when most of its markets were stronger, MacMillan earned C$0.50 a share or C$66 million.
"There are going to be a lot of angry shareholders. It will get nasty," said analyst Sam Magid of Salman Partners.

MacMillan has been under intense pressure from shareholders disappointed by its performance. Speculation has swirled since last summer that the company would embark on a major restructuring that might include the departure of chief executive Bob Findlay.
MacMillan chief financial officer Glenn Ferguson declined to comment on the earnings forecasts or the size of the provisions.

But he said management was recommending to the board that charges be taken. "It is management's intent to make some provisions for some asset writedowns and severation (severance) costs," he said, declining to elaborate.

Industry sources said the charges would cover one-time costs at a U.S. subsidiary that makes synthetic roofing material, a writedown on boilers at the company's problem-plagued Powell River, British Columbia paper mill and some layoffs.

Analysts said MacMillan's operating loss in the fourth quarter partly reflected poor industry-wide conditions in pulp, paper and packaging. But the company was saddled by high costs, especially in its paper division, they said.

Analysts and industry sources said MacMillan was also experiencing steep losses at its American Cemwood Corp unit in Oregon, which makes synthetic cedar shake roofing material. The subsidiary dominated the market until the entry of Re-Con Building Products Inc three years ago.
American Cemwood has "lost a huge market share. Their time is definitely limited," said one industry executive.

So far, the company -- which has said it was reviewing all options to increase value -- has taken some steps including selling its shipping division for C$108 million in a deal expected to close in March.

But analysts said those were not enough to appease shareholders. "Clearly there will be additional pressure put on management over the next six months," said a Toronto analyst who asked not to be identified. "People are expecting more restructuring."
Magid of Salman Partners said he expected MacMillan would need to cut its C$0.60 a year dividend or raise up to C$400 million in debt in 1997.
MacMillan was down 0.05 to 17.55 in early trading today in Toronto and was unchanged at 13 on Nasdaq (corrects from "off 1/4 to 13-3/4 in New York").
